notes.meaning: An angel who poured out God's judgment invites John to witness the sentence against the great prostitute. In the Bible, a prostitute often represents people or cities that turn away from God to worship idols. Her sitting on many waters shows that her corrupt power stretches across many nations and rivers.

Earthly kings and common people have joined in her false worship and ungodly ways. The world has become drunk on her sins, losing its moral senses just like people confused by too much wine. Idolatry and worldly pleasure have blinded them to God's truth.

The Holy Spirit carries John away in a vision to a barren wilderness. There he sees a woman sitting on a bright red beast covered with names that insult God. The terrifying beast has seven heads and ten horns, showing that brutal political empires support and carry this false religious power.

The woman is dressed in royal purple and bright scarlet cloth, glittering with gold, pearls, and costly jewels. This lavish display makes her look wealthy and important to the world. Yet the golden cup in her hand is full of filthy, repulsive sins and false worship in the eyes of God.

The woman has a mysterious title written on her forehead, just as ancient prostitutes often displayed their names. She is called Babylon the Great, the mother of every kind of idol worship and moral filth on the earth. This means she is the primary source of religion that leads people away from the true God.

John sees that the woman is drunk, not with wine, but with the blood of God's holy people and martyrs. Martyrs are faithful witnesses who chose to die rather than deny Jesus. John is utterly shocked and horrified to see such religious splendor combined with bloody cruelty.

The angel asks John why he is so astonished by the sight. He promises to explain the hidden meaning of both the woman and the seven-headed, ten-horned beast that carries her. God wants his people to understand the true nature of evil so they are not deceived by its power.

The beast once existed, disappeared, and is about to rise from the dark pit before facing total destruction. Earthly people whose names are not written in God's Book of Life will be amazed by this fake comeback. Evil powers may seem to rise from the dead, but their end is already decided by God.

Understanding this vision requires godly wisdom and spiritual insight. The angel explains that the seven heads represent seven mountains where the woman sits. To John's first readers, this clearly pointed to the famous city of Rome, which was built on seven hills.

differ.view: The seven mountains are symbolic of great world governments rather than literal hills.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic writers note that Vatican City rests on a single hill across the river from ancient Rome, so this vision cannot describe the Catholic Church.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars observe that first-century coins and writers constantly celebrated Rome as the city on seven hills, pointing directly to the Roman Empire.

notes.meaning: The seven heads also stand for seven kings or great world empires. Five of these mighty rulers have already fallen, one is currently in power, and the last has not yet arrived. When that final ruler comes, God will allow him to reign for only a short time.

differ.view: The five fallen kings represent past world empires (Egypt, Assyria, Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece), Rome is the one that is, and a future revived Roman empire is the seventh.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: The kings are a historical line of Roman emperors, with the first five running from Augustus to Nero, Vespasian as the ruler in power, and Titus as the one who would reign only briefly.

notes.meaning: The beast that once lived and then vanished acts as an eighth king, though he belongs to the earlier seven. He gathers all the cruelty and rebellion of previous empires into himself. Even with all his terrifying strength, he is marching straight into final ruin.

The ten horns represent ten future kings who have not yet received their kingdoms. In God's timing, they will be given royal power to rule alongside the beast for a single brief hour. Their power is temporary and strictly limited by God's plan.

These allied kings share one common goal and purpose. They willingly surrender all their national power and military strength to the beast. Earthly leaders often unite in evil, gladly giving up their freedom to fight against God's truth.

This united empire launches an attack against the Lamb, who is Jesus Christ. The Lamb wins completely because he is the supreme Lord of all lords and King over every king. Alongside him stand his faithful, chosen followers, sharing in his grand victory.

The angel tells John that the waters beneath the prostitute represent the huge crowds of the world. They are made up of many different nations, tribes, and languages. This shows that her corrupt teachings and deceptive power have spread all over the earth.

The beast and the ten allied kings will suddenly turn on the prostitute and hate her. They will rob her of her riches, strip her bare, tear her apart, and burn her with fire. Evil alliances always crumble, and corrupt world powers end up destroying the very partners they once used.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some Catholic commentators interpret this as Rome turning against Jerusalem, fulfilled when Roman armies burned the city and its temple in AD 70.

notes.meaning: This dramatic turn of events happens because God himself places the plan into the hearts of the kings. He uses their united support of the beast to carry out his own righteous judgment until his words come true. Even when wicked rulers think they are in charge, God is working out his sovereign will.

The angel concludes by stating that the woman is the great city ruling over the kings of the earth. In John's day, this was ancient Rome, the center of imperial rule and persecution. No matter how mighty an earthly city seems, God will hold it accountable for its sins.

differ.view: Reformed interpreters historically identified this city and harlot as Papal Rome, arguing that the medieval Roman church claimed rule over kings and misled nations with false teachings.
Many evangelicals believe Babylon represents a future worldwide false religion or a rebuilt literal city that will dominate the earth during the end times.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic scholars hold that the city represents pagan Rome or first-century Jerusalem, which shed the blood of apostles and prophets in ancient times.
